project.name: Fiction Workbench
project.summary: A local, single-user workspace for planning and writing long novels. It organises outlines, characters and chapters as Markdown and JSON files, and compiles a bounded writing brief that the user hands to Codex. The app itself never calls an AI API. Every statement below was checked against the source code.

flows.name: Create a novel project
flows.scene: On the Project Library page you fill in a title, a project ID and a language, then click Create.

steps.title: Submit the form
steps.what: The form sends its fields to a backend function and shows any field errors next to the inputs.
tech: Draws the form and shows the result message
The form calls the backend function createNovelProjectAction directly
files: Project Library page: project list and the create form
Home page that shows the library

steps.title: Validate the input
steps.what: Every field is checked against a set of rules before anything touches the disk. Bad input returns an error per field; the chosen genres and styles must exist in the shared library.
tech: Rule sheet for the input: ID format, title length, locale format
Turns storage errors into a readable message
files: Rule for safe project IDs (lowercase letters, digits, hyphens)

steps.title: Build the project manifest
steps.what: Creates the project's identity card (project.json) with a schema version, timestamps and the list of folders a novel project needs.
tech: Stored in project.json so future versions can upgrade old projects

steps.title: Write it all-or-nothing
steps.what: Everything is first written into a hidden temporary folder. Each path is checked to stay inside that folder. Only when all files are in place is the folder renamed to its real name; on any error the temporary folder is deleted.
tech: A half-created project can never appear
assertPathWithinRoot rejects any path that escapes the folder
files: All reading and writing of project folders

flows.name: Save a chapter
flows.scene: You edit the outline, text or summary of a chapter and click Save.

steps.title: Send the text and its fingerprint
steps.what: The editor sends the text plus the fingerprint (revision) of the version you opened.
tech: Holds the editor text and shows “unsaved changes”
files: persist: runs when you click Save

steps.title: Check the input
steps.what: The request must name a valid project, volume and chapter, the text must be under 4 MiB, and the fingerprint must be 64 characters long.
files: Backend entry for chapter actions (not readable in this test: path too deeply nested)

steps.title: Refuse if the file changed elsewhere
steps.what: The store re-reads the chapter and compares fingerprints. If the file on disk changed after you opened it (for example, Codex wrote to it), saving is refused with “changed on disk, please refresh”.
tech: revision() turns a file's text into a 64-character fingerprint
files: All reading and writing of chapters

steps.title: Write safely, then update metadata
steps.what: The text goes to a temporary file, is flushed to disk, then renamed over the real file. Then meta.json gets a new updated time. New fingerprints go back to the editor.
tech: writeStaged: the real file is never half-written
files: All reading and writing of chapters

flows.name: Hand a chapter to Codex
flows.scene: On a chapter page you open the Codex writing panel and click Copy.

steps.title: Compile a bounded brief
steps.what: The app collects only what this chapter needs: the chapter outline; project, world, style and volume notes; one character card per selected character (with their relationships and personality-based guidance); a short prose sample; and the ending of the previous chapter.
tech: The brief is assembled on the server when the chapter page loads
Merges profile, personality and relationships into one card per character
files: Gathers the materials for one chapter

steps.title: Trim the previous chapter
steps.what: Only the ending of the previous chapter is passed on: the whole text if it is 1,200 characters or less, otherwise about the last 1,000 characters, cut at a paragraph or line break.
tech: endingExcerpt counts Unicode characters and looks for a break

steps.title: Turn it into an instruction
steps.what: The IDs and word targets are validated again, and the brief is serialised as JSON between <compiled_chapter_context> tags, with the name of the Codex skill to call and the one file it may write.
tech: Validates IDs and the word range
The brief is machine-readable for the Codex skill
files: Builds the text you paste into Codex

steps.title: Copy to clipboard
steps.what: Clicking Copy puts the instruction on the clipboard and shows a confirmation.

steps.title: Codex writes the chapter
steps.what: In VS Code, Codex runs the project's own skill. It re-checks every ID and path, refuses links that escape the project, and writes only that chapter's content.md. It does not change outlines, metadata or status.

steps.title: Back in the app
steps.what: When you reopen the chapter, the editor shows the new text with a new fingerprint. If you had unsaved edits open from before, saving them is refused (see Flow B), so Codex's text is not overwritten by accident. Chapter status changes only when you change it.
files: All reading and writing of chapters

flows.note: The chapter page file that wires steps 1–4 together (src/app/projects/[projectId]/volumes/[volumeId]/chapters/[chapterId]/page.tsx) could not be read in this test because the path is too deeply nested for the file bridge.

flows.name: Delete a chapter and restore it
flows.scene: You delete a chapter, then open the project's recycle bin and restore it.

steps.title: Confirm by typing the ID
steps.what: Deleting requires typing the full chapter ID. A mismatch stops the deletion.
tech: The user must type the exact ID
files: All reading and writing of chapters
recoverablyDeleteChapter: stops if the typed ID does not match

steps.title: Move, don't delete
steps.what: The chapter folder is moved into .fiction-workbench/recovery/chapters/<volume>/<chapter>-<time>. Every folder on the way is checked to be a real folder inside the project, not a link pointing elsewhere.
tech: Moves the whole folder in one step
Reject symbolic links and paths outside the project
files: All reading and writing of chapters

steps.title: Restore
steps.what: Restoring checks that nothing with the same ID now sits in the original place (it never overwrites), moves the folder back, and updates the book structure. If updating the structure fails, the move is undone and the item stays in the recycle bin.
tech: Re-validates the stored JSON before using it
Moves the folder back if the second step fails
files: Backend entry for recycle bin actions

flows.name: Delete a whole project
flows.scene: On the Project Library page you delete a project.

steps.title: Confirm by typing the ID
steps.what: You must type the exact project ID.

steps.title: Delete permanently
steps.what: The project path must sit directly inside the projects folder; then the whole folder is removed. There is no recycle bin for whole projects.
tech: Refuses anything that is not a direct child of the projects folder
files: All reading and writing of project folders

flows.note: The README says deleted projects are moved to fiction-projects/.trash/. The code deletes them permanently, and the success message says “permanently deleted”. The code is correct; the README is out of date.

quiz.question: When you click Save in the chapter editor, how does the screen reach the backend? How can you tell which files run in the browser?
quiz.answer: The editor calls a Next.js Server Action. Files that start with "use client" run in the browser; actions.ts files start with "use server" and run only on the server.

quiz.type: Why data is stored this way
quiz.question: Why does this project use Markdown and JSON files instead of a database?
quiz.answer: So that the user and Codex can open and edit the same files in VS Code, every change is readable, and each chapter is a folder that can be moved to the recycle bin and back. JSON holds the structured parts and is checked with Zod.

quiz.question: Codex rewrites a chapter while you still have the old version open in the editor. What happens when you click Save?
quiz.answer: The save is refused: the fingerprint of the file on disk no longer matches the one you opened, so you are asked to refresh.

quiz.question: Restoring a chapter fails half-way. Is anything lost?
quiz.answer: No. If the book structure cannot be updated, the folder is moved back into the recycle bin and an error is shown.

quiz.question: How is Codex kept from writing outside one chapter?
quiz.answer: The app gives it a bounded brief with exact IDs and one output path; the Codex skill re-validates IDs and paths, rejects links, and may only write that chapter's content.md.
